info.title: Port Rust API Gateway
info.summary: REST edge for the Port Rust social backend
info.description: Complete checked-in REST contract for the Axum gateway. Every operation documents its request body, path/query/header inputs, authentication mechanism, success body, common error envelope, correlation response header, and special cookie/redirect/binary responses. Authorization is represented by security schemes rather than a duplicate Authorization header parameter. User-Agent is supplied automatically by the client, and X-Forwarded-For is infrastructure-owned and must only be injected by a trusted reverse proxy. Internal service-to-service APIs use protobuf/gRPC and are documented in proto-reference.md.

get.description: Returns DEAD_LETTERED account-deletion sagas oldest first by the time the current status was last updated. The bounded page defaults to 20 and accepts 1–100 items. Pass both afterUpdatedAt and afterSagaId from nextCursor to continue. This read-only endpoint never retries cleanup; use the saga detail route to inspect current steps before an explicit operator resolution. Because sagas can transition into or out of DEAD_LETTERED while paging, this is not a frozen snapshot.

post.description: Only a DEAD_LETTERED saga can be restarted. Requires a client-generated resolutionId reused with the exact same request after an uncertain response, a reason, and an identifier for a protected evidence record. The reference is syntax-checked, not resolved externally; do not include secrets or evidence contents. AuthService atomically records an immutable resolution receipt and reviewer-attributed audit event, starts a fresh bounded attempt cycle for incomplete steps, and fences results from older worker generations. Reusing the resolution ID with different request values conflicts. The 202 response reports the saga's current state; acceptance does not mean cleanup is complete. The attempt ceiling is deployment-configured and total administrator retry cycles are not globally capped.

post.description: Only RETRY_EXHAUSTED commands can be replayed. Requires a client-generated resolutionId reused with identical request fields after an uncertain response, a reason, and an identifier for a protected evidence record. The reference is syntax-checked but not resolved against an external evidence system. The Gateway appends an immutable reviewer-attributed audit record and requeues the original decision with a fresh attempt cycle; it does not change the decision payload or bypass PostService idempotency. Each cycle is limited to eight attempts; the total number of admin-authorized cycles is not capped.

get.description: Returns the Gateway lifecycle state and its best evidence-backed outcome. For the ten allowlisted PostService, FriendService, ProfileService, and Gateway-owned moderation-report mutations, it also performs a read-only owner-receipt lookup. A verified complete receipt can resolve COMMITTED only when operation ID, actor, and versioned scope match the Gateway journal. NOT_FOUND is absence of evidence, not proof of non-commit; UNAVAILABLE, MISMATCH, and incomplete receipts remain unresolved. HTTP status alone never proves rejection: REJECTED_BEFORE_COMMIT requires evidence that an exact owner-backed route did not cross its mutation boundary or an audited manual resolution. The response contains receipt metadata only, not the actor ID, command, idempotency key, fingerprint, or outcome body. An unknown Gateway operation ID is a 404.

post.description: Appends an immutable, admin-attributed disposition for an UNKNOWN operation. Requires a reason and a reference to a protected evidence record. The Gateway journal is not rewritten, no response is manufactured, and the mutation is never rerun. Corrections must name the current resolution id and append a new revision. An identical retry by the same reviewer returns the existing record.

get.description: Returns the authenticated caller's lifecycle state, evidence-backed outcome, response status, timestamps, and whether a response snapshot remains replayable. The lookup is actor-scoped; another caller's operation is indistinguishable from an unknown id. UNKNOWN does not prove rejection and does not authorize a new command. For a documented idempotency-enabled mutation, preserve the original key and payload; use only that operation's documented recovery path. The endpoint never returns the stored response, request details, owner-receipt data, or operator evidence.

post.description: A successful form returns a nonce-CSP HTML page that submits only code and state to the same-origin completion endpoint, with a manual Continue button if JavaScript is disabled. 200 does not mean authenticated. The original SameSite=Lax state cookie may be absent on this cross-site POST. The page neither sets nor clears cookies. Provider cancellation/error, code+error, unsupported providers, malformed/ambiguous/oversized forms and unsupported media types return a generic JSON 400 without downstream Auth calls. Optional id_token/user are ignored. All responses use no-store, no-referrer and nosniff; HTML also forbids framing and external resources. Do not log or persist code/state/form bodies or put them in URLs.

post.description: Submitted by the Gateway-origin intermediate page. Requires exactly one original oauth_state_apple cookie equal to the form state; missing, mismatched, other-provider or duplicate cookies return 400 before Auth. Auth atomically consumes provider/state before exchanging the code and rejects expired, consumed or racing state. Success sets the refresh HttpOnly cookie and clears the Apple state cookie; refreshToken in JSON is empty. Responses use no-store/no-referrer/nosniff. A timeout may follow state consumption or session creation: never automatically resubmit, infer rollback or generate replacement state to retry this callback. GET callbacks remain available unchanged.
